Modified response using SLOOS lens:
- The FOMC cut the target range to 1.75–2.00 percent to support expansion amid muted inflation and softer business investment/exports.
- July 2019 SLOOS signals tighter credit supply to businesses: banks tightened standards on C&I loans and on construction and land development (CRE) loans and tightened other terms across firm sizes; demand for construction/land development loans was weaker. These developments reinforce downside risks to business fixed investment already noted by the FOMC.
- Consumer credit conditions are mixed: banks reported tightening standards for other consumer loans with generally unchanged demand, while government-backed mortgage segments saw stronger demand with largely unchanged standards. This suggests household spending support persists but with some incremental headwinds outside government-backed categories.
- Net: Monetary easing and continued reinvestments are supportive, but SLOOS shows tightening and weaker demand in key business and CRE segments that could dampen the transmission of easier policy. Compared with the prior assessment, the outlook is more cautious.
